node.title: Re: is there a way to ensure some code is the last thing that is run?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Hi [morgon],

Based on your [id://1180914|example code], would it be correct to assume that the problem is happening because of circular references? If so, then tracking those down might be a good start, it should lead you to the culprit code.

I looked into tracking circular references, unfortunately it seems that [mod://Devel::LeakTrace] and [mod://Devel::LeakTrace::Fast] don't compile on modern versions of Perl/glib, [mod://Devel::Leak] seems a bit too low-level, and [mod://Devel::Cycle] requires you to specify which variables to check for cycles, which can be difficult if you have lots of objects being created. So far, the "best" thing I have found seems to be [mod://Devel::Leak::Object], which can override [doc://bless].

Also, I fiddled around with [mod://Devel::Gladiator] and has_circular_ref from [mod://Data::Structure::Util], which seems to support more types of data than [mod://Devel::Cycle]. Note that it appears to be important to limit the inspection to those things that we're actually interested in, in this case objects - just blindly using it on everything that walk_arena() returns leads to errors, and I even got some segfaults at one point. But the following seems to work, at least on your example code:

use Devel::Gladiator qw/walk_arena/; use Data::Structure::Util qw/has_circular_ref/; use Scalar::Util qw/blessed/; sub find_all_cycles { my $all = walk_arena(); for my $sv (@$all) { # limit search to objects next unless blessed($sv); warn "Has circular references: $sv\n" if has_circular_ref($sv); } @$all=(); } END { find_all_cycles() }

Hope this helps,
-- Hauke D
